subject: Greenline MAP: security gate clarifications, DPA redlines, and retention
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@greenlinepay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Greenline MAP: security gate clarifications, DPA redlines, and retention

Alex —

Following up from last week's demo: attaching a draft mutual action plan (MAP) that scopes the evaluation and the close timeline. Before we finalize the MAP milestones we want to lock the security/compliance gates so your legal and security teams have what they need to move this along. High-level asks from Greenline's list we heard: SOC 2 evidence, SIG/CAIQ responses, and DPA scope + retention details.

Quick questions to help us line up the intake:
- SOC 2: do you need the full Type II report or is the Redwood SOC 2 summary + control matrix sufficient for procurement?
- SIG/CAIQ: would you prefer the spreadsheet we fill out or a short call to walk through high-risk controls?
- DPA redlines: please confirm the signers and whether you require a Data Processing Addendum with data residency clauses.
- Retention: what's the target retention period for transactional data vs. logs/metrics? (We can propose defaults and make them configurable in Dedicated/Private.)

Proposed timeline in the MAP (draft):
- Week 0: finalize DPA redlines + SOC2 evidence request list
- Week 1: SIG/CAIQ delivery + security Q/A
- Week 2: Procurement review, legal signoff
- Week 3: Contract execution + start of pilot (if all gates pass)

I've attached: the MAP draft, our SOC 2 summary, and an initial DPA with proposed redlines for your review. If it helps, we can run a 30-min sync on Thursday to go over any high-risk items and signers.

Thanks — looking to keep momentum so we can hit the pilot-date in the MAP.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0198

From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@greenlinepay.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Greenline Legal <legal@greenlinepay.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Mar 2028 11:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Greenline MAP: security gate clarifications, DPA redlines, and retention

Ben —

Thanks for the MAP draft and the attachments. A few clarifying items from our side so we can scope legal/security review:

1) SOC 2 — we typically require the full SOC 2 Type II report for production-critical vendors. However, if you can provide a SOC 2 summary + control matrix and a timeline for delivering the Type II, that will help procurement decide on conditional approval for pilot. Please confirm the audit period and whether production infrastructure is in scope.

2) SIG/CAIQ — spreadsheet is fine. If you can pre-fill high-risk controls (data encryption at rest, key management, service isolation for multi-tenant), our security team will triage. We may still request a quick walkthrough for any responses marked 'partial'.

3) DPA — legal will want to review redlines. We also need to know if you offer data residency guarantees (US-only) for logs or transaction data.

4) Retention — our default is: transactional data retention = 7 years (financial regs), logs for troubleshooting = 13 months, metrics/aggregates = 5 years. Can Redwood support a configurable retention policy at the account level? If not, we need to know default retention and whether we can request exceptions for longer-term archival.

5) Signers — we'll need the DPA signed by someone with contracting authority on your side and our VP of Security + Head of Compliance on ours. Please confirm the signer's title and contact.

If you can address these points and push an updated DPA + filled SIG spreadsheet, we can aim to complete legal/security review within two weeks. Otherwise, procurement will likely push the SOC 2 Type II requirement before execution.

Alex
Alex Mercer
Director of Platform Engineering, Greenline Payments
alex.mercer@greenlinepay.com

Ben / team —

Thanks for the heads up and lemme summarize next steps from the security side.

SOC 2: production in-scope (confirmed). Our latest Type II report completes coverage through 2027-10-31; we can provide a SOC 2 summary + control matrix today and commit to delivering the full Type II report under NDA within 10 business days. Action: see attached redwood_soc2-summary-20280310.pdf (control mappings highlighted).

SIG/CAIQ: I've prefilled the spreadsheet for the high-risk rows (encryption, key management, tenant isolation, incident response). Items marked as 'partial' are:
- Multi-tenant isolation: logical separation with strict RBAC and encryption, but not fully dedicated physical hosts in Hosted tier.
- Third-party subprocessors: we list them and provide SOC2 coverage where applicable.
Action: sig-caiq-responses-20280314.xlsx attached. I recommend a 30-min walkthrough with Greenline security on Monday to walk through the partials.

DPA / retention: proposed defaults we support across Redwood hosted:
- Transactional/financial data: default retention = 90 days in hot storage; archival options available (S3 cold) for up to 7 years on request with contractual addendum.
- Logs/traces (for debugging): 13 months (rolling).
- Aggregated metrics: 5 years.
We can include contractual language to allow Greenline to request 7-year archival for transaction data (add-on professional services + storage costs). For Dedicated/Private deployments, data residency (US-only) is available.

DPA redlines: Marissa, legal notes below (high level) — please review and propose final redline for Redwood signatory: Director of Contracts or VP Legal (depending on monetary threshold).

Next steps / suggested schedule:
- Thu 15 Mar: deliver SOC2 summary + prefilled SIG (done/attached)
- Mon 19 Mar: 30-min security walkthrough with Greenline (booked by Ben)
- Tue 20 Mar: Greenline legal to review DPA redlines; Redwood to provide final counter if needed
- By Fri 23 Mar: aim for procurement/legal conditional signoff so pilot can begin Week of 26 Mar

Attachments: redwood_soc2-summary-20280310.pdf, sig-caiq-responses-20280314.xlsx (attached to thread)

I'll draft the brief talking points for the walkthrough and share them in the Drive link. Let me know if we need to include any engineering folks on the call for architecture deep-dive.
